regimen_profiles.regimen_role: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Palbociclib slows cell-cycle progression while the hormone partner reduces oestrogen signalling. The aim in this advanced-disease pathway is cancer control, with treatment and response reviewed over time.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Palbociclib: Hormone signalling can activate cyclin-D/CDK4/6. Palbociclib blocks this control point, helping keep susceptible cells from progressing through the cell cycle. Combining it with endocrine therapy acts on both the hormonal signal and downstream cell division. Your endocrine partner: An aromatase inhibitor lowers oestrogen production; fulvestrant acts at the oestrogen receptor. These are alternative partners here, not an instruction to take both. The partner’s dose, monitoring and injection or tablet schedule must be confirmed.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Take palbociclib for 21 days, then have 7 days without palbociclib. The aromatase-inhibitor tablet continues every day, or fulvestrant injections follow their separate schedule. The week off applies to palbociclib, not automatically to the hormone treatment.
key_points: NCCP 00414 a: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic disease with an aromatase inhibitor. NCCP 00414 b: the same receptor/disease setting with fulvestrant in women who have received prior endocrine therapy. Pre/perimenopausal women also need an agreed ovarian-suppression plan.
Usual palbociclib dose: 125 mg once daily on Days 1–21 of a 28-day cycle; reduced prescribed doses are 100 mg or 75 mg.
Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable. There is no fixed adjuvant course in NCCP 00414. Blood results or symptoms may change the dose or postpone the next cycle.

The same low count can lead to a different action at Day 1 and Day 15 of the first two cycles. Dose decisions also depend on fever/infection, recovery, severity and current dose. A clinician must confirm a restart; the patient timeline is an explanation, not permission to self-adjust treatment.
Palbociclib does not have the routine ECG timetable used for ribociclib. ECG or echo is arranged if symptoms, another medicine or individual cardiac risk make it appropriate.

Bone-health monitoring belongs to the endocrine partner, ovarian suppression and personal fracture risk. If taking an aromatase inhibitor, agree the baseline bone-density assessment and follow-up plan with the team; palbociclib itself has no fixed DXA interval.
Patient schedule is relative and requires no date input. It does not authorise treatment or restart.
NCCP v 5 a capsule instructions require food. EMA includes tablets that allow food or no food; confirm formulation rather than silently generalising.
NCCP expects no renal reduction in dialysis; EMA has insufficient dialysis data. Explicit oncology/pharmacy review is retained, with no invented numeric reduction.
Grade 3 atDay 1 andDay 15 ofcycles 1–2 have different actions. Isolated grade 3 count without timing returns review; it does not force unrelated inputs.
Fever/infection grading input means grade 3 neutropenia plus fever≥38.5°C and/or infection. Patient fever instructions must follow local safety-netting, not wait for 38.5°C.
No routine palbociclib-only ECG, echo, fixed 3 monthly CT or tumour-marker schedule is mandated by NCCP.
All clinical-use, consultant-validation and oncology-pharmacy-validation flags remain false.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Postmenopausal HR-positive / HER2-negative advanced breast cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Exemestane lowers oestrogen production while everolimus blocks an intracellular growth pathway that can contribute to endocrine resistance. The aim in this setting is to control cancer and delay progression.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Postmenopausal HR-positive / HER2-negative advanced breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Everolimus: Everolimus binds the intracellular protein FKBP12; this complex inhibits mTORC1, affecting protein synthesis and growth signalling. This pathway can support endocrine resistance, which explains pairing it with an oestrogen-lowering medicine. The same pathway operates in normal tissues, contributing to mouth ulcers, infection risk and metabolic changes. Exemestane: After menopause, aromatase in tissues converts androgen precursors into oestrogen. Exemestane is an irreversible aromatase inhibitor that reduces this supply to hormone-sensitive cancer cells. It does not directly switch off functioning ovaries; the menopausal indication must be confirmed.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Both tablets are taken every day continuously. There is no planned week off. A four-week blood-test review is a monitoring interval, not a stop-and-restart treatment cycle.
key_points: NCCP 00322a: postmenopausal hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without symptomatic visceral disease after recurrence or progression following a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor.
Usual starting doses: everolimus 10 mg once daily and exemestane 25 mg once daily; the prescribed everolimus dose may be lower.
Continue while the treatment is helping and side effects remain manageable, according to the consultant plan. This advanced-disease regimen has no fixed adjuvant completion date.

If everolimus is interrupted or reduced for toxicity, NCCP says exemestane may continue; the treating team must confirm the plan for each medicine. Do not stop both automatically or restart everolimus yourself. Everolimus can increase toxicity around radiotherapy and impair wound healing: agree a specific plan before radiotherapy or surgery.
NCCP 00322 does not mandate routine ECG or echocardiography. Cardiac tests should follow symptoms, comorbidities and other treatments, rather than a copied HER2-treatment schedule.
Exemestane can reduce bone mineral density. Review fracture risk and arrange DXA and bone protection when indicated. This regimen does not specify a single repeat-DXA interval for everyone.
NCCP 00322 is not an exemestane monotherapy card and not an adjuvant endocrine regimen; do not inherit those eligibility lists.
The old encoding had only two generic rules and no operative ANC/platelet or detailed toxicity decisions. This audit adds 77 source-linked rules with component-specific actions.
NCCP Table 3 uses CTCAE v3.0. Do not infer its metabolic/stomatitis grade solely from a generic CTCAE v5 label.
For grade 3 febrile neutropenia, the NCCP restart ANC is ≥1.25×10^9/L with no fever, different from the afebrile neutropenia threshold ≥1.
Exemestane continues through everolimus interruption or modification unless a separate clinical reason changes the plan.
Child-Pugh A/B/C: NCCP everolimus 75%/50%/25% of original dose. EU SmPC adds benefit-risk qualification and 2.5 mg/day maximum for Child-Pugh C. No automatic combined hepatic/toxicity restart dose.
No automatic imaging schedule is invented. The clinical team must define the response-assessment plan; pulmonary symptoms warrant urgent investigation.
Radiotherapy is not a routine phase of this regimen. Show any actual radiotherapy on a parallel individual plan, with an explicit joint decision about everolimus timing.

Independent clinical and oncology-pharmacy validation remains pending. The current-catalogue NCCP v4 PDF and EMA product information (updated 20 November 2025) were downloaded and cross-checked, with visual review of their toxicity tables.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive or HER2-low breast cancer, within the NCCP prior-treatment criteria
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Aim to control cancer growth, reduce cancer-related symptoms and prolong disease control. Individual benefit and duration vary; trial averages cannot predict one person's outcome.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive or HER2-low breast cancer, within the NCCP prior-treatment criteria
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (Enhertu): Enhertu links an antibody that recognises HER2 with deruxtecan, a cell-killing medicine. After uptake into the cell, the payload inhibits topoisomerase I and interferes with DNA replication. The released payload can also affect nearby tumour cells. This targeting does not spare every healthy cell, which is why blood counts, nausea, lungs and heart function still need attention.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: One infusion on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle. The next infusion is normally three weeks later. A delayed appointment is rescheduled by the team; patients do not calculate catch-up doses.
key_points: NCCP00776a: unresectable/metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer after at least one anti-HER2 regimen. NCCP00776b: unresectable/metastatic HER2-low breast cancer after chemotherapy for metastatic disease, or recurrence during or within six months after adjuvant chemotherapy.
Usual starting dose 5.4 mg/kg intravenously on Day 1 every 21 days; prescribed reductions are 4.4 then 3.2 mg/kg

Treatment continues while it controls the cancer and side effects remain acceptable. This advanced-disease regimen has no automatic one-year completion date. A good scan does not by itself instruct a treatment break.

Enhertu is different from trastuzumab and trastuzumab emtansine (Kadcyla); they are not interchangeable. Carry the supplied Enhertu lung-safety alert card. The team may pause treatment while investigating suspected lung inflammation; symptomatic drug-related ILD requires permanent discontinuation under the protocol.

NCCP specifies echo/MUGA before treatment and every 12 weeks. With uninterrupted three-week cycles, week 12 is approximately before cycle 5 and week 24 before cycle 9. Delays do not reset the elapsed-time monitoring clock. regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Olaparib (Lynparza): BRCA1 and BRCA2 help cells repair breaks in DNA. Some cancers with these changes rely more heavily on other repair routes. drug_profiles.name: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (Enhertu)
drug_profiles.mechanism: Enhertu links an antibody that recognises HER2 with deruxtecan, a cell-killing medicine. After uptake into the cell, the payload inhibits topoisomerase I and interferes with DNA replication. The released payload can also affect nearby tumour cells. This targeting does not spare every healthy cell, which is why blood counts, nausea, lungs and heart function still need attention.

drug_profiles.name: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy)
drug_profiles.mechanism: The antibody component recognises Trop-2 on cancer cells. Its linked SN-38 payload interferes with topoisomerase I, an enzyme involved in managing DNA during copying, which can damage dividing cells. Healthy tissues can also be affected, particularly blood-forming cells and the gut; being antibody-directed does not mean it is free of chemotherapy-type effects.

drug_profiles.name: Olaparib (Lynparza)
drug_profiles.mechanism: BRCA1 and BRCA2 help cells repair breaks in DNA. Some cancers with these changes rely more heavily on other repair routes. Olaparib inhibits PARP activity and traps PARP on DNA, making it harder for those cancer cells to survive DNA damage. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, which is why regular blood counts matter.
